name: @w6w-apps/ollama
description: Run prompts, chats and embeddings against your own Ollama server and manage its models.

w6w.longDescription:
Ollama runs open large language models on hardware you control, and this app talks to your own server: you give it the host, port and scheme when you connect, and it calls Ollama's REST API directly. A workflow can generate text from a prompt, continue a chat conversation, produce embeddings, and ask for structured JSON that matches a schema, with images for vision models and sampling options such as temperature, seed and context size. It can also look after the server itself: list the installed and the currently loaded models, inspect one's capabilities and context length, pull a new model, copy or delete one, and unload a model to free memory.

Because the server is yours, reachability is the part to get right. A LAN or localhost address works only when workflows run on the same network, through a self-hosted runner; hosted runs need a tunnel or a reverse proxy with a public hostname. Ollama listens on 127.0.0.1 unless started with OLLAMA_HOST=0.0.0.0, and has no authentication of its own, so the API key is optional and only sent when a proxy in front of the server needs one. Every call is non-streaming.
